physical meaning / why it may indicate d: Overall vibration energy; grows as defects enlarge and friction/impacts increase.
Largest instantaneous shock; sensitive to single strong impacts (also to noise spikes).
Total excursion; similar to peak but based on the signed range.
Impulsiveness. About 0 for smooth Gaussian vibration, rises when sharp impacts appear (spalls, cracks).
Asymmetry of the amplitude distribution; one-sided impacts change it.
Peak-to-average ratio; rises early with isolated impacts, falls when damage becomes continuous.
Waveform shape; changes when the amplitude distribution departs from Gaussian.
Sharpness of impulses relative to the mean level.
Peak relative to a low-order mean; emphasises rare large peaks (classical incipient-fault indicator).
Total spectral power (Parseval: equals variance); tracks overall energy growth.
Centre of gravity of the power spectrum; moves when high-frequency resonances are excited.
Bandwidth of the spectrum; broadens with damage.
Dominant frequency (shaft harmonics vs structural resonance).
Fraction of power at low frequency (shaft rotation harmonics; shaft speed is 25-30 Hz).
High band, where impact-excited resonances appear.
